bounds: One real browser LoginAuth instance, two overlapping expired-session reads, one refresh request and nine finite outcomes: living session, direct or HttpOnly-proxy recovery, explicit 401, transient 503, missing recovery credential and sign-out before a direct refresh returns. The loopback server controls the actual HTTP response; Chromium provides real cookies, localStorage and Web Locks.
limitations: This proves SDK custody and result transitions for the finite responses. It does not prove backend JWT signing, refresh-family database transactions, cross-tab scheduling, production OAuth, or server-side revocation.
The request bound applies to overlapping reads while one refresh is pending. A later read after a transient failure may legitimately start a new refresh.
Progress requires browser dispatch and the finite server response to arrive. Fairness of read, sign-out where selected, and settlement is explicit.

assumptions: Weak fairness of the selected browser read, explicit sign-out and finite HTTP settlement. Server response termination is assumed.
